# gottem

> Universal scraper. One CLI and one Rust library that talks to every major scraping vendor through a single tiered ladder. Cheapest-first by default; escalates on failure; races or hedges when latency matters. Powered by [spider](https://github.com/spider-rs/spider).

Built around two concepts: **routes** are data (TOML rows describing a vendor endpoint), **adapters** are code (a small finite set of protocol families). Adding a new vendor is a config change, not a release. 22 builtin routes across 13 vendors span T0–T9 of the cost/capability ladder.

## Crates

- [gottem-core](crates/gottem-core/src/lib.rs): traits + types + orchestrator + retry strategies + waterfall stats.
- [gottem-adapters-spider](crates/gottem-adapters-spider/src/lib.rs): single-page fetch via `spider::page::Page::new_page` (T0-T3).
- [gottem-adapters-http](crates/gottem-adapters-http/src/lib.rs): `direct_http` / `http_json` / `http_jsonl_stream` for cloud REST APIs.
- [gottem-adapters-chrome](crates/gottem-adapters-chrome/src/lib.rs): `chrome_cdp` adapter — remote browser via WebSocket DevTools Protocol (T8).
- [gottem-adapters-captcha](crates/gottem-adapters-captcha/src/lib.rs): 2Captcha submit + poll for solver chains.
- [gottem-adapters-browseruse](crates/gottem-adapters-browseruse/src/lib.rs): Browser Use Cloud AI agent (submit + poll, returns final output).
- [gottem-routes-builtin](crates/gottem-routes-builtin/routes/): embedded vendor TOML, feature-gated per vendor.
- [gottem-cli](crates/gottem-cli/src/main.rs): `gottem` binary — `fetch` / `probe` / `routes`.

## CLI

```sh
gottem fetch URL [--mode ladder|race|hedge] [--budget-mc N] [--tier-min N --tier-max M] [--require-js] [--routes a,b,c] [--format content|json] [--show-meta]
gottem probe URL [--tier-min N --tier-max M] [--min-bytes 500]
gottem routes list                       # tabular catalog
gottem routes show <route-id>            # full route detail
gottem routes validate                   # check env vars per route's auth
gottem --config routes.toml fetch URL    # layer custom routes on top of builtin
```

Hedge mode adds `--hedge-delay-ms` and `--hedge-count`. Race mode honors `--routes a,b,c`.

## Tier ladder

- **T0**: free local HTTP via spider::Client
- **T1–T2**: same + proxy rotation
- **T3**: local headless Chrome (chrome adapter)
- **T4** ($0.001/page): Firecrawl, Spider HTTP, ScrapingBee, ZenRows basic
- **T5** ($0.005): + JS render
- **T6** ($0.0075): + residential proxy
- **T7** ($0.008–$0.010): smart unblockers — Spider Smart, Zyte API, Brightdata Unblocker
- **T8** ($0.010–$0.015): browser-as-a-service — Browserless, Brightdata Scraping Browser, Spider Browser Cloud
- **T9** ($0.02+): last resort — Apify, Oxylabs, 2Captcha solver chains, Browser Use AI agent, Browserbase

Within a tier, cheapest first; Spider's `priority = 0` wins cost ties.

## Routes are data

```toml
[[route]]
id          = "firecrawl.scrape"
adapter     = "http_json"
endpoint    = "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1/scrape"
method      = "POST"
tier        = 4
cost        = 10                # milli-cents
timeout_ms  = 30000

[route.auth]
kind = "bearer"
env  = "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"

[route.body]
kind     = "json"
template = '''{"url":"{{url}}","formats":["markdown"]}'''

[route.parse]
kind = "json_path"
path = "$.data.markdown"

[[route.validate]]
kind = "min_bytes"
n    = 500
```

Five adapter kinds cover essentially every scraping vendor in the wild:

- **`direct_http`** — plain GET/POST
- **`http_json`** — POST JSON, parse JSON (Firecrawl, Zyte, Brightdata, Apify, Oxylabs)
- **`http_jsonl_stream`** — POST JSON, parse streaming JSONL (Spider only)
- **`chrome_cdp`** — WebSocket CDP (Browserless, Brightdata Scraping Browser, Spider Browser Cloud)
- **`captcha_2captcha`** + **`browser_use`** — submit + poll protocols baked in

## Three orchestration modes

- **`ladder`** (default): cheapest first; escalate on failure (status, validation, network error). Stops at first valid response, budget ceiling, or `--max-retries`.
- **`race`**: fire all selected routes in parallel; first valid response wins; rest cancelled via `CancelToken`.
- **`hedge`**: primary at t=0, backups at t = i × `--hedge-delay-ms`. Adaptive delay shrinks when latency variance is bad. First valid wins.

## Waterfall promotion (learned ordering)

After enough samples for a `(route, domain)` pair, the orchestrator skips the ladder warmup and starts at the proven route directly. Score combines cost / latency (EMA) / reliability (success rate) / confidence (log sample count). Cheapest qualifier wins on ties. Configurable via `WaterfallConfig`. Bounded memory (default cap 1M entries) with automatic stale-entry eviction.

## CAPTCHA chains

`captcha.2captcha` is a route — call it like any other route, but it returns a captcha TOKEN instead of page HTML. Compose: scrape primary → detect challenge → call captcha route with `siteKey` + `captchaType` in `req.extra` → replay original URL with token embedded.

## Per-request cost forwarding

`ScrapeResponse.cost_actual_units` + `cost_actual_unit` carry the vendor's reported per-request cost (ZenRows `Zr-Cost` header, Spider JSONL `$.costs.total`, etc.). Static `cost_milli` is always present; actual is `Option` because not every vendor exposes it.

## Force a single provider for testing

`gottem fetch URL --routes <id> --mode race` runs only that route. Useful to verify one vendor works for one URL without the ladder.

In the library: `Orchestrator::execute_once(&route, &req, 0, &cancel)` is the primitive — no ladder, no race, no waterfall promotion. Single attempt.
